audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is described only as a 'grab-stun'. The condition on the stun is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text: Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, and if enemies were only on one side they are slowed instead of stunned. A Mel standing on the same side of Sett as her own minions eats a slow, not a stun, and walks away from the Haymaker that was supposed to follow. A Mel who lets him step between her and the wave eats the full stun. That single positioning rule is the difference between the two outcomes and it is currently absent.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker stuns only with enemies on both sides of him — stay on the same side as your wave and it degrades to a slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells Mel to chip Sett constantly without saying what that chip does to his Haymaker.
audit.why: Haymaker passively stores the damage Sett TAKES as Grit, and on cast expends all of it for a shield plus a punch dealing true damage in the centre. Mel's whole plan is repeated chip, so her poke is also the fuel for the one spell in his kit that ignores her resistances. That does not mean stop poking — it means poke and step back rather than poke and stand there, and expect a bigger punch the longer the trade ran.
audit.corrected: Say that every point of poke he absorbs is stored Grit for the true-damage centre of Haymaker.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Sett four of seven stages while the recorded win rate is 55.56% for Mel — the packet flags this directly.
audit.why: Facebreaker is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and its range is 490; Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 1000 range and Radiant Volley reaches 950. Through levels 4-5 Mel's root returns roughly five seconds before his engage does, which is not a stage he owns — it is a stage decided by whether she wastes the snare. At first item her Blackfire Torch spike arrives against a champion whose first bruiser item does nothing about the 460-unit gap he still has to walk. Levels 3 and 6 stay his: rank-1 snare against a fresh Facebreaker, and The Show Stopper.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 becomes Skill; First item becomes Mel. Sett keeps Level 3 and Level 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere, so 'only step up when his W bar is empty and E is on cooldown' has nothing behind it.
audit.why: Facebreaker 16s at rank 1 against Solar Snare 11s at rank 1 is the whole early lane in one comparison, and Haymaker's 18s at rank 1 is the second clock.
audit.corrected: Give both numbers where the advice is given.

edits.before: His passive double-punch and stored-W grit out-sustain your short trades while you have no dash to disengage his walk-up.
edits.after: Facebreaker is 16s to your snare's 11s, so your root returns first — but every point of chip you land is Grit loading Haymaker.

edits.before: His first-item bruiser spike plus a stored W still bursts you through any poke, and one E-grab ends the trade.
edits.after: Blackfire Torch outpaces his first bruiser item: he still has to walk 950 to reach a 490-range Facebreaker.

edits.before: Once Sett has W stored and E online he can grab-stun you and dump a true-damage smash — this is where his grit trade overtakes your poke.
edits.after: Once Grit is stored and Facebreaker is up he can pull you in and land a true-damage centre punch — his Haymaker trade overtakes your poke.

edits.before: Hold W to eat his engage and never get caught flush — kite, detonate Overwhelm with R from range
edits.after: Stay on the same side of him as your wave — with nothing behind him Facebreaker slows instead of stunning

edits.before: Bait out your E root, then E-grab you and unload a fully-stored true-damage W smash
edits.after: Bait your snare, then Facebreaker you across the wave and unload a stored Haymaker

edits.after: Soak your poke on purpose — the damage he takes is the Grit that loads Haymaker

edits.before: Level 1 is yours: at 550 range with your ranged auto and the first Radiant Volley bolt you chip Sett while he can only walk up to CS, and he has nothing stored in his W yet. But respect how fast this flips — the moment Sett has W charged and E online, every step you take into his E range risks a grab-stun into a fully-stored true-damage smash that erases your HP bar. Save Solar Snare to root him OUT of his grab, not to poke; a misused E lets him walk up free and W-smash you. Don't greed a Q at close range — he just eats it on his passive grit and grabs you.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: at 550 range with your ranged auto and the first Radiant Volley bolt you chip Sett while he can only walk up to CS, and Haymaker has nothing stored yet. But respect how fast this flips — the moment Grit is charged and Facebreaker is up, every step inside 490 risks a pull into a true-damage centre punch. Save Solar Snare to root him out of Facebreaker range, not to poke. And know the price of chip: every point of damage he absorbs is stored as the Grit that fuels that punch, so poke and step back rather than stand and trade.

edits.before: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Rebuttal for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: 16s at rank 1 against your 11s snare, 490 range, and it only stuns with enemies on both sides of him. - Haymaker is 18s and fuelled by the damage you deal him. - Budget Rebuttal for emergencies.

edits.before: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — once he's marked deep, your execute math starts working. Track Facebreaker before stepping up.
edits.after: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — but Grit is stored from damage he takes, so your chip loads Haymaker while it loads your execute.

edits.after: Track Sett’s Facebreaker: it stuns only with enemies on both sides of him — stay on your wave's side and it lands as a slow.
